screen12-a1.glyph: three horizontal lines of decreasing length
screen12-a1.description: three stacked lines control in the top-left corner of the toolbar
screen12-a1.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Open menu" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen12-a1.convention_relied_on: three stacked horizontal lines (hamburger) is an established convention for opening the app's navigation menu — my reading, confidence high
screen12-a1.initial_rationale: unlabeled, but the hamburger glyph is a widely-known convention; common-icon exemption applies pending the behavioural test
screen12-a1.deciding_evidence: same control as screen1-a1 (identical appearance, words and position in the same repeated state); tested once there and the verdict carried: tapping the hamburger opened the side navigation panel, exactly what the convention promises

screen12-a2.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc "Filter" — read only to know what to tap for and watch for; not used in the verdict
screen12-a2.convention_relied_on: a sliders glyph is an established 'filter / adjust' convention — my reading, confidence medium

test_cases.expected_result: a filter choice for the list appears
test_cases.confirms_if: something other than a filter opens

screen12-a2.deciding_evidence: the sliders glyph opened a list filter, matching the convention
